messages.subject: D-RUG and Tea Time this Thursday!
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG and Tea Time this Thursday!
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. Additionally, if there are topics you would like to see someone do a deeper dive on, let us know!

There is also Tea Time in the DataLab classroom from 1-2pm Thursday if you are looking to take a break from work with tea (or coffee) and cookies.

Zoom at this link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.subject: Upcoming R workshops at UC Davis
messages.subject_clean: Upcoming R workshops at UC Davis
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

While D-RUG hosts regular weekly meetings in the Datalab Classroom, there are also periodic workshops in the same space. The following R-related workshops are coming up in the second half of this quarter (and even an introductory Python workshop for the sickos out there). Registration is required but all are free:

- November 14-15: Introduction to Remote Computing and HPC  <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/intro-hpc-2024?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events>
We’ll provide an overview of HPC terminology, architecture, and general workflows, and guide learners through how to set up and use SSH to log in and transfer files, how to install software with miniconda, how to reserve computing time and run programs with SLURM, and execute shell commands that are especially useful for working with servers. As we learn we’ll practice accessing and computing on remote servers using the UC Davis HPC Core Facility’s new “Hive” cluster.

- November 18: Using Campus HPC for Large-Scale Data Analysis with OpenOnDemand <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/hpc-openondemand-2024?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events>
Are you working on a research project but finding that your data is too big for your laptop, or that your code must run for a long time? You need more compute power! This one-day workshop will cover the basics of remote computing for researchers using the UC Davis HPC. We'll be using OpenOnDemand, which makes it easy to use HPC without being a unix expert!

- November 20: The Modern Practical Scholar: Distilling a research domain with bibliometric analysis in R <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/modern-practical-scholar-3-bibliometrics?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events>
This is the third in a 3-part "Modern Practical Scholar" in person workshop series designed to share inclusive, equitable, and sustainable practices for knowledge acquisition. We'll focus on setting up and using free, open source software to swiftly gather, organize, and curate research literature. These workshops are applicable for any level of scholarship, and may be attended as a series or separately.

- December 11: Introduction to Reproducible and Collaborative Research Practices <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/reproducible-research-intensive-2024?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events>
In conjunction with the following R and Python Basics series, the goal of this workshop is to increase research integrity via exposure to basic command line tools and version control (Git), collaborative cloud tools (GitHub), programming (R or Python), and data and software management best practices.

- December 12-13: R Basics: Introduction to Programming for Researchers <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/r-basics-2024?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events>
This two-day workshop provides an introduction to using the R programming language for reproducible data analysis and scientific computing.  Topics covered include programming basics, how to work with tabular data, how to break down programming problems, how to organize code for clarity and reproducibility, and best practices for data, code and software management.

- December 12-13: Python Basics: Introduction to Programming for Researchers <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/python-basics-2024?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events>
This two-day workshop provides an introduction to using the Python programming language for reproducible data analysis and scientific computing. Topics covered include programming basics, how to work with tabular data, how to break down programming problems, how to organize code for clarity and reproducibility, and best practices for data, code and software management.

-Wes

messages.subject: D-RUG and Other Events this week
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG and Other Events this week
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGies!

We have quite a bit going on this week.

There will be D-RUG at from 10am-noon virtually and in person, as well as Tea Time at 1pm and Co-working from 2-4pm. HOWEVER, All of those events will be in Library 362 (the conference room) instead of in the classroom.

This is because DataLab is running a Intro to Remote Computing Workshop <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/intro-hpc-2024?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=UC+Davis+Library+Events> this Thursday and Friday. If you have ever thought "this R code is taking a really long time to run. There must be a better way" or maybe "I ran out of memory again!", this is the workshop for you. You will need to have some familiarity with the command line for this workshop, but don't worry DataLab has you covered there as well with the Intro to Unix Command Line <https://ucdavisdatalab.github.io/workshop_introduction_to_the_command_line/> reader.

If you need more computing resources, but the command line seems a bit to scary, we have Using Campus HPC for Large Scale Data Analysis with OnDemand <https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/hpc-openondemand-2024>. This workshop is next Monday (December 18) and will show you how to use high performance computing resources from the comfort of an RStudio interface.

Zoom at this link: https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09

Happy Coding!
Your CooRdinators
